_readme: The one repair the Triage Repair run (scripts/triage_repair.py, DRE-8647) gives a card, chosen by which writer put it in Triage. One row per unit config/triage-reasons.json declares — tests/test_triage_repair_every_arrival.py fails on a declared unit with no row here, so a Triage writer added tomorrow cannot arrive unhandled. `marker` is what the writer leaves on the card, and exactly one of: `hold`, the reason of its live `🔒 hold:` stamp; `tag`, the tag its note opens with after its mark (`🧹 planning-stall-park:`); `description`, a phrase in the description of a card it creates straight into Triage. A card is matched by its live stamp first, then by its newest pipeline-authored note carrying a tag, then by its description; a card matching no row is `rewrite`. Rows that share a marker share a repair, because the marker cannot tell them apart. `repair` is one of: `rewrite` — the planner answers the park reason and the card goes to Planning (select's `repair` action, `escalate` when a finding names a choice only the CEO can make, `replan` for a card with children); `replan` — an epic's bound rewrite, then Planning; `relabel` — the planner names one key of config/repo-map.json in repo.txt, and the card gets that repo: label, its hold lifted and a move to Planning; `none` — no planner runs, and the claim is followed at once by an `unrepairable` receipt saying `why` (`{ids}` is the claimed ids no relation holds).

rows.why: the description claims a dependency on {ids} that the board does not hold; only its author can reword the line
